#### General Updates: Comms/Ping Updates

The new functionality for Praise is intended to be a quick way to celebrate a team kill or an incredible shot without needing to use voice chat. We won't judge you if you use it sarcastically too, like when your teammate fat fingers their ult in spawn. We didn't want to change your Comms Wheel customizations when we added Praise, so instead of replacing something on the wheel that you might have added years ago, we made the Comms Wheel function almost identically to the Ping Wheel. Keep in mind that you can revert the Comms Wheel to its original functionality by changing a single setting! Alongside our commitment to expanding the game's story, our narrative and sound teams have been working hard to record more great voice lines that let you express your personality through our heroes. We'll continue to expand on your communication options by adding more contextual lines over time.

Praise

* "Praise" added as a new default function of the Comms Wheel.
* Tapping the Comms Wheel button now tells your allies how awesome they are with Praise voice lines that are unique to each hero.
* By default, the Comms button functionality now mimics the functionality of the Ping Button, meaning there is a very short delay (.18 seconds by default) between pressing the button and the wheel opening.
* This new functionality can be disabled in the Options with the setting "Enable Quick Press Praise". The delay can be modified with the setting "Comms Wheel Press Delay".
* This short delay is immediately canceled when any mouse movement or right stick movement is detected, for players that want to flick to a Comms Wheel option.
* Praise can be assigned to the Comms Wheel in the Options, but it is not assigned to the Comms Wheel by default.

New Contextual Voice Lines and Functionality

* Heroes now emit voice lines that suggest setup locations to their team when players use neutral pings during the Setup Phase while defending in Attack/Defend modes.
* Heroes now have more specific internal monologue voice lines for when they request healing and no supports are available to help.
* Heroes on defense in Escort and Hybrid are now more likely to notice when a payload is being pushed by a sneaky player and call it out with a voice line.
* Heroes will now automatically call out to their team with a voice line when they detect an invisible hero nearby (Sombra).
* This uses the same cooldown and tuning as when heroes detect Widowmaker aiming at them and warn their allies with "sniper" voice lines.
* Heroes can aim at an allied Jetpack Cat and ping her to request a pick up at their location with a voice line.
* The "On My Way" Comms now prints an ETA in seconds in text chat when aiming at an allied hero based on the speaker's speed.

Bug Fixes

* The Ping System's spam protection now works in the Waiting For Players phase of a match.
* Supports no longer hear the healing ping sound effect when another support on their team pings an injured ally.
* Thanking a support for the "Not So Thankless" challenge should now more reliably count for challenge completion.

#### General Updates: Advanced Info Panel

* Added all 5 new heroes.
* All Cleanses in the Advanced Info Panel have been separated between Lesser Cleanses which are much more common and Greater Cleanses which are more rare and can cleanse Stuns. The definitions of these keywords have been updated.

* Added the following new Keywords to abilities where relevant:
  + Aura - An Energy ability that gains resource whenever dealing damage or healing.
    - Example: Mizuki's Remedy Aura
  + Break - Removes Tether effects.
    - Examples: Jetpack Cat's Catnapper, Lifeweaver's Life Grip, Reinhardt's Charge, Roadhog's Chain Hook
  + Displace - Prevents a hero from taking actions while moving them, interrupts Channeled abilities, and is not Cleansable.
    - Examples: Doomfist's Rocket Punch, Reinhardt's Charge, Roadhog's Chain Hook
  + Heat - Ceases to function when the Heat gauge is full and cools off automatically when not firing.
    - Examples: Emre's Siphon Blaster, Orisa's Augmented Fusion Driver
  + Immobilize - Removes control of hero movement.
    - Examples: Hazard's Downpour, Lucio's Soundwave, Wrecking Ball's Piledriver, Zarya's Graviton Surge
  + Tether - Attaches a hero to a location or hero within a radius until the tether ends.
    - Examples: Jetpack Cat's Lifeline, Jetpack Cat's Catnapper, Mauga's Cage Fight, Mizuki's Binding Chain

While almost all recent development on this feature was focused on providing accurate information about the new heroes, our efforts to help explain the game's most nuanced mechanics have continued here with the addition of new Keywords. If you haven't used this system much, keep in mind that all of the Keyword definitions can be viewed in a match or in the Practice Range when hovering over an ability!

#### Core Game Updates

Core Game Modes

Clash Removed

As we move into 2026, the team is carefully looking at what maps and modes provide players with the best long term experience in Overwatch. We want to lean into the content that players engage with the most while also providing a high level of gameplay variety. After all, variety in our maps and modes is a core pillar on our design team, and that will never change. It is also important that the variety we offer resonates with our players. Unfortunately, even after some adjustment, Clash hasn't been hitting the mark.
We love the maps that we made for Clash. They will remain in Stadium and we still may see them return in the future. We have some amazing new maps lined up for the next year and our reworks will continue...and get bigger. Redesigns that completely change how certain areas of our maps play are coming soon. As we look into the future of our game, we will continue to curate our map roster in the ways we feel offer the best experience. We look forward to sharing more news about all the upcoming maps and modes coming to Overwatch.

#### Competitive Play Updates

Rank Reset

* With 5 new heroes joining the fray, alongside several new perks and balance changes for existing heroes, this soft reset is designed to put players on an even playing field and give them a chance to climb in a chaotic new environment where everyone is learning together!
* All ranks in Role Queue and Open Queue in Competitive Play have been reset to Unranked, and all players will need to complete their respective 10 placement matches for each role.
* Hero Skill Ratings have also been soft reset.
* This Rank Reset did not change the Rank Distribution, so players can expect to see a similar number of players in each Rank once everyone is calibrated again.
* Rewards:
* Crimson Wolf replaces Galactic as this year's Competitive Weapon Variant and will be available to be unlocked with Competitive Points after the first two weeks of the season!
* Galactic Weapon Variants join the Gold and Jade Weapon Variants as Legacy Rewards.
* Achieving Diamond or above in Role Queue or Open Queue will now unlock Doomfist's Crimson Wolf skin.
* All Competitive Points earned in the 2025 Competitive Year have been converted into Legacy Competitive Points.

Top 500 Challenger Updates

* We heard your feedback about the name change, and we agree "Top 500" was too iconic to abandon, so we've combined the old and new names.

* Sort By Rank:
  + The Top 500 Challenger leaderboard can now be sorted by Rank.
    - Rewards are awarded based on Challenger Score.
    - Only players with enough Challenger Score to be on the leaderboard are sorted by Rank.

Rule Changes

* Challenger Score is no longer awarded based on the highest ranked player in the match.
  + Challenger Score is now always awarded based on your own rank.
* Diamond removed from Top 500 Challenger eligibility
* The challenge required for Top 500 Challenger eligibility has been swapped from Seasoned Competitor to Adept Competitor.
* Challenger Score deduction on loss increased from 33% to 40%

We quickly realized this design choice was a mistake when we heard the player feedback that the leaderboard should prioritize rank much more highly than it did at Season 20 launch, and this choice meant that the highest ranked players were often donating a considerable amount of Challenger Score in their games to lower ranked players. This change means that we can tune the highest ranks to gain considerably more Challenger Score and ensures that only the highest ranked players benefit from these rewards. These increased payouts for the highest ranks now account for both the difficulty of maintaining these ranks and the increased queue times associated with these ranks.

Since we redistributed the Ranks in Season 18 to allow for more players at our highest Ranks (Master, Grandmaster, Champion) we agree with the community feedback that Diamond is not prestigious enough for the leaderboard.

This change means that 250 total wins in Competitive Play are required to appear in Top 500 Challenger instead of 750. With Challenger Score as a requirement, the 750 win requirement was unnecessarily high.

Rewards

* Player Icons return as a reward for Top 500 Challenger.
  + New icons will be available at each Rank Reset, meaning that a new icon becomes available to earn every 3 seasons.
  + Placing in Top 500 Challenger during the Rise of Talon Season 1, 2, or 3 will grant the Conquest Top 500 Challenger player icon.

Social Links Update

* We've been working to expand the tech that allows our Community Team to add social links of prominent players to the leaderboard.
  + Updates in Season 21 should allow for considerably more players to have their social links added to this feature.
* We've discovered that some older Battlenet accounts without a birthdate set are not able to view social links.
  + This feature is designed to be for players that are 18+, but the lack of a birthdate is currently preventing these older accounts from viewing the social links.
  + We're continuing to investigate solutions to this problem and we apologize to those players that are unable to use this feature at this time.

  + Combined Role and Open Queue: Reduced from 5000 to 2000.
  + Each Individual Role: Reduced from 4000 to 1500

We hope these updates show our commitment to updating this system based on player feedback, but this is also a good time to address some of the feedback we've heard that probably isn't a viable path for us today. We've heard some of our highest rank players request that we decay ranks at the start of each season like we did before the launch of Overwatch 2. Before Season 9 of Overwatch 2, Rank and MMR were not directly linked and could diverge considerably. After Season 9, we committed to Rank and MMR being linked in the Core game because we believe showing you the most accurate representation of your skill is important to the competitive integrity of the system. That's still the case today, and it's why the type of pseudo-Rank decay that was applied to high rank players at that time (artificially displaying them at a lower SR than their MMR) is not an option for us today. If we used that type of decay today, we'd be lowering the MMR of all of the highest ranked players every season. This has a lot of knock on effects, but it would be effectively creating more severe versions of the Rank Resets we do every 3 seasons today, but only for players above a specified MMR. We see this as undesirable because of the negative impact it would have on match quality every season for our highest ranked players. We appreciate all of your feedback about this feature so far and we'll continue to listen for ways we can improve it going forward.

#### Heroes Update: Sub Roles

* Tank Role Passive
  + Reduced ultimate charge is granted from healing and damage received.
    - Ultimate Generation Reduction: -40%
  + Base health increased in Role Queue game modes.
    - Bonus Health: +150
  + Knockback Resistance and Critical Damage Resistance removed from the role passive.
* Damage Role Passive
  + Removed
  + The following effects that were previously granted by the Damage Role Passive are now baseline for all heroes.
    - In-Combat Healing Reduction on Damage: -30%
    - Reduced effectiveness against Tanks: -15%
* Support Role Passive
  + Removed
  + Global regeneration after 6 seconds remains unchanged.

The role passive system has undergone a significant revision, introducing multiple categorized passives within each role. Heroes are now assigned to a subcategory within their role, granting them a new passive that is more closely aligned with their intended playstyle. This approach aims to enhance gameplay depth and role identity for each hero.

Looking ahead, we will closely monitor the effectiveness of this new system. Our ongoing plan includes evaluating its impact and making future adjustments as needed. This could involve balancing individual subroles, reassigning heroes to different subroles, or even introducing entirely new subroles to better support the evolving needs of the game.

#### Stadium Competitive Update

* Powers are now granted in rounds 1, 2, 4, and 6

We're testing a format change in Competitive that we heard suggested frequently during the revert from the Best of 5 format. This change should be a good middle ground, keeping the faster power progression so your builds come online faster while maintaining the Bo7 format that allows for more time to adapt to the enemy and create memorable comebacks. We also think this has the ability to increase comeback potential, particularly in Round 2. Previously, falling behind in Round 1 meant that Round 2 will feel like a repeat of Round 1, but with the enemy having more items, since early on you often don't have enough currency to meaningfully change your build. However, being able to select a Power means being able to get a large power spike in your build and more tools to adapt and fight back with in the pivotal early rounds, even when behind. We'll be keeping a close eye on this change, so let us know your feedback!
